name: Accessibility Audit
description: Audit a digital product against WCAG and real assistive-technology workflows, then verify fixes instead of checking boxes.

tasks.name: Define audit scope
tasks.objective: Identify platforms, user journeys, conformance target, browsers/devices, assistive technologies, dynamic states, documents/media, and known accessibility risks.

tasks.name: Run automated and structural checks
tasks.objective: Use automated scanners and source inspection for semantics, names/roles/values, contrast, labels, landmarks, heading structure, forms, ARIA misuse, parsing, and common detectable failures. Treat scanner coverage as partial.

tasks.name: Test keyboard and assistive technology
tasks.objective: Test complete workflows with keyboard-only navigation, focus order/visibility, screen reader, text zoom/reflow, motion preferences, touch targets, error recovery, and relevant voice/switch input.

tasks.name: Test dynamic states and content
tasks.objective: Inspect modals, menus, live regions, loading/error/empty states, authentication, time limits, drag interactions, media alternatives, charts, PDFs/documents, and responsive variants.

tasks.name: Prioritize defects
tasks.objective: Map findings to WCAG success criteria where applicable, user impact, frequency, blockers, affected journeys, reproducible steps, and likely root cause. Separate conformance failure from broader usability concern.

tasks.name: Verify remediation
tasks.objective: Retest exact failing paths and adjacent components after fixes using the same assistive technologies and viewport conditions. Close only with evidence.

tasks.name: Publish audit and regression plan
tasks.objective: Deliver reproducible findings, screenshots/DOM or code context, severity, criterion references, remediation guidance, verified status, and a regression checklist for design/development QA.
